Description: Fragments of a Hebrew Psalms copy from Qumran Cave 4, in Herodian script. Like 4Q83, it places Psalm 31 directly before Psalm 33, an order different from the Masoretic Psalter. Unprovenanced post-2002 fragments sometimes claimed for this manuscript (e.g. a Psalm 9 fragment) are NOT counted here, as they have no Qumran provenance. Preserved-passage ranges for this manuscript are given in English (KJV) numbering; the manuscript itself carries no modern psalm numbers. Publish-prep note: every PreservedPassages range in this entry was re-versified to English (KJV) numbering against DJD XVI (Skehan/Ulrich/Flint) via Ulrich, The Biblical Qumran Scrolls (2010), Index of Biblical Passages (MT/BHS numbering), with the SBL Appendix B table. First-pass conversions (over-length ranges only, from the earlier cleanup): Psalms 31:24-25 to 31:23-24. Final pass verified every remaining range as already correct English numbering (untitled psalms and first-clause-title psalms do not shift).
Significance: An early Hebrew witness to the Psalms, predating the medieval Masoretic manuscripts by about a thousand years. Its chief value is textual: it shows which psalms and which readings were already in circulation in the Second Temple period, and, where its psalm order differs from the Masoretic Psalter, that the order of the Psalter was not yet fully fixed.
